title: ClipForge Hook Strategy Library

source_document.title: DAS HOOK-MANIFEST
source_document.source_scope: The five strategy families and 50 templates come from the source PDF. Integration/validation metadata below is added for ClipForge use.

design_intent.primary: Use the library as strategy guidance after neutral research. The model should write a fresh, topic-specific hook from researched facts.
design_intent.secondary: If free strategy-guided generation fails quality validation, adapt one of the source templates more tightly.
design_intent.last_resort: Use a source template as a strict fill-in pattern only when both primary and guided fallback fail. Never use an unsupported statistic/trend just because a template contains one.

recommended_pipeline: 2. Perform neutral research first; do not search to justify a preselected hook.
3. Extract hook signals: strongest fact, misconception, contrast, consequence, verified number, verified trend/social proof, self-check, viewer relevance.
5. Generate 3-5 fresh hook candidates using the best-fitting family/families.
6. Validate factual support, natural language, strategy fit, question-echo, source contamination, and hook/body progression.
7. If a candidate is strong, select it.
8. If not, use guided_fallback with one suitable fallback template.
9. If guided fallback still fails, use strict_template_fallback.
10. Optionally run targeted follow-up research for the selected hook claim before final script generation.
11. Build the body to pay off the selected hook immediately.
source_principles: Neutral informational hooks are often less reaction-provoking than clear statements or positions.
Provocation should attack an opinion, habit, assumption, or way of thinking - not a person.
A strong hot take must contain substance and remain defensible when challenged.
Templates are a starting point, not the end product; context and what is actually being discussed matter.
The strongest hooks are not necessarily the loudest; the viewer should take away a useful new perspective.

do: Prefer concrete, defensible claims over vague hype.
Let the LLM write natural German or English from the pattern rather than copying the source wording.
Use viewer relevance when it is a real consequence, experience, risk, benefit, decision, cost, or mistake - not merely a pronoun.
Make the answer/body progress beyond the hook instead of repeating it.
do_not: Do not treat any number, percentage, prevalence, trend, or business claim inside the template bank as factual evidence.
Do not force every topic into a provocative family.
Do not generate fake controversy, fake social proof, fake statistics, or fake personal stakes.
Do not prepend mechanical wrappers such as “Für dich heißt das” or “This affects you” merely to simulate relevance.
Do not literal-translate German templates into English when the result sounds unnatural.

primary_strategy_generation.instruction: Use strategy family semantics and research signals. Generate original language.

guided_fallback.instruction: Choose one semantically suitable template, adapt its structure to the topic, then rewrite naturally. Keep evidence gates active.

strict_template_fallback.instruction: Fill only supported placeholders. If a template requires evidence that is unavailable, skip it and try another. If none fit, fall back to a safe factual hook or the original question/title.

strategy_families.source_trigger: Eine klare, angreifbare Meinung, die sofort Zustimmung oder Widerspruch auslöst.
strategy_families.primary_pattern: Challenge a common belief, habit, assumption, or default framing with a specific, defensible reframe.
use_when: Research supports a genuine contrast or defensible contrarian interpretation.
There is a common assumption, habit, or framing worth challenging.
The claim can be defended with the researched facts.
avoid_when: The only way to make it provocative is to exaggerate or invent controversy.
The hook would attack a person rather than an idea, habit, or assumption.
The topic is purely factual and has no defensible reframe.
strategy_families.evidence_policy: Strong claims must be supportable by the research. Broad quantifiers such as “most” require evidence or must be softened into an explicitly framed opinion.

strategy_families.source_trigger: Eine Selbstprüfung, bei der der Zuschauer wissen will, ob er selbst den Fehler macht oder betroffen ist.
strategy_families.primary_pattern: Turn a researched mistake, blind spot, or decision into a self-check the viewer can immediately apply to themselves.
use_when: The topic contains a concrete mistake, misconception, blind spot, or self-test.
The viewer can meaningfully evaluate their own behavior, decision, knowledge, or setup.
The challenge leads directly into useful information.
avoid_when: There is no real self-assessment to make.
The hook would shame or insult the viewer.
A percentage or prevalence claim would need to be invented.
strategy_families.evidence_policy: Any prevalence/statistical framing must be externally verified. The self-check itself may be qualitative if it accurately follows from the topic.

strategy_families.source_name_de: Social Proof – die Angst, etwas zu verpassen
strategy_families.source_trigger: Die Angst, etwas zu verpassen, das plötzlich andere wissen, nutzen oder tun.
strategy_families.primary_pattern: Use a real, researched pattern of adoption, behavior, discussion, or group difference to create a credible “what do they know?” gap.
use_when: Research shows a real trend, adoption pattern, common behavior, or meaningful group difference.
The social signal is directly relevant to the topic.
The viewer can learn something concrete from the comparison.
avoid_when: There is no verified trend or group behavior.
The hook relies on vague claims such as “everyone is switching”.
The social signal is unrelated to the actual answer.
strategy_families.evidence_policy: Trend, popularity, adoption, “top performers”, and “everyone” claims require research support. Never manufacture social proof.

strategy_families.source_trigger: Eine konkrete Zahl oder Größenordnung macht die Bedeutung sofort greifbar.
strategy_families.primary_pattern: Lead with a verified number, ratio, magnitude, time, cost, probability, or measurable contrast whose implication matters to the topic.
use_when: Research contains a strong, relevant, verified number.
The number creates useful scale or consequence rather than decoration.
The number can be stated accurately and with the right scope.
avoid_when: The number is only illustrative or comes from an unverified template.
The statistic needs missing population/time/context to sound impressive.
strategy_families.evidence_policy: Hard gate: every numeric/statistical claim must be supported by researched evidence with matching value and context. Numbers in this library are template examples, never evidence.

strategy_families.source_trigger: Eine direkte “Nicht X, sondern Y”-Aussage, die eine Annahme des Zuschauers angreift, nicht die Person.
strategy_families.primary_pattern: Directly replace a likely wrong explanation with a stronger researched explanation: not X, but Y.
use_when: Research supports a clear misconception or causal reframe.
The contrast can be expressed simply and specifically.
The correction gives the viewer immediate value.
avoid_when: The contrast would be false or oversimplified.
The wording becomes a personal attack.
The hook is confrontational only for style, without a real misconception.
strategy_families.evidence_policy: Both sides of the reframe must be defensible. Do not turn nuance into a false binary.

implementation_notes.load_behavior: Load once as static, non-secret application configuration. Do not hardcode all templates inside Python source.
implementation_notes.prompt_usage: Pass compact strategy summaries plus only the few best-matching fallback templates to the Content Director; do not dump all 50 templates into every prompt.
implementation_notes.english_support: Strategy metadata is language-neutral. For English generation, preserve rhetorical intent and rewrite natively in English.
implementation_notes.future_extension: Additional strategy families can be added later without changing the existing template IDs.
